subject: Clarify: session-floor accounting and fractional-token handling for Atlas Retail

Subject: Quick billing questions before procurement call

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement is reviewing the contract and a couple of technical billing items came up that I want to make sure we understand before the SOW: 1) How do you actually bill when a single logical session spans multiple requests (we have lots of short interactions that together form a long conversation)? 2) If a single response is tokenized into fractional billing units (e.g., we see partial tokens based on your meter), do we get prorated credit or is there rounding up to the minimum?

Also, can you show a simple example invoice line for a week with lots of microcalls to illustrate the math? If possible, attach a sample. We need this for our finance team to justify the estimated run-rate.

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, details below and an attached worked example (billing_examples.xlsx).

1) Session vs microcall: We group requests into a billing "conversation window" based on a configurable inactivity threshold (default 15 minutes). Calls within that window are considered the same session for "session-floor" purposes (one floor applied per active session).

2) Fractional tokens: Our meter reports token usage at call granularity and charges in 1-token units with a minimum per-call floor. We then apply session-level smoothing: if multiple calls in the same conversation produce fractional remainders, we amortize leftover fractional portions toward the session floor before rounding to invoiceable tokens. Practically that reduces overcharging for many short calls.

I've cc'd Neha from finance to confirm the commercial consequences (discounting/credits). Let me know if you want us to walk through the spreadsheet on the procurement call.

Thanks,
Sergio
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai

Attachment: billing_examples.xlsx (spreadsheet with per-call token counts, session grouping, round/credit columns)

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, Priya Shah <pshah@atlasretail.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T10:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick billing questions before procurement call

Hi all — adding a bit more color from the billing side and proposed contract language to avoid surprises: 

- Floor application: For every active conversation window we apply a session floor equal to the equivalent of 8 tokens (configurable by SKU/commit). That means if the summed invoiceable tokens across calls in the window are below the floor we invoice the floor.

- Fractional handling: We do not invoice fractional tokens separately. We compute per-call tokenization precisely, sum across the session window, then round to the nearest whole token. If after rounding the total is still below the session floor, we bill the floor. If the customer has a committed package or reserved capacity, the floor is used to allocate usage against the commitment first (not billed as overage).

- Smoothing & credits: For short-call-heavy workloads like Atlas's, our recommendation is to enable "session smoothing" which applies amortization across a 24-hour horizon for orphan fractions — that is, small fractional leftovers are carried and netted before final invoice rounding. We typically enable smoothing for enterprise pilots (no extra cost) and include it in AR-committed deals.

Proposed contract snippet (suggested):
"""
Billing: usage is measured per API call and tokenized. Tokens are summed across conversation windows (15-minute inactivity default). Usage is rounded to whole tokens for invoicing; for windows with total tokens below the session floor, the session floor (8 tokens unless otherwise specified) will apply. Committed packages consume session floors against committed units first. Fractional remainders are netted across the invoice period with session smoothing applied to eligible accounts.
"""

I ran the numbers in the attached spreadsheet for a representative week from Atlas (sheet 'Atlas-week-sample') — that's the same file Sergio attached. Key result: with smoothing turned on, estimated monthly cost is ~6% lower vs raw per-call rounding. Without smoothing the session floor still protects us but you may see higher overage variability.

Happy to review line-by-line on Wednesday's call.

Cheers,
